Prefer this when scaffolding — \" +\n        \"each separate write_file costs a whole round trip, so a ten-file \" +\n        \"skeleton written one call at a time is ten times slower and dearer.\",\n      parameters: {\n        type: \"object\",\n        properties: {\n          files: {\n            type: \"array\",\n            description: \"Files to write, up to 30.\",\n            items: {\n              type: \"object\",\n              properties: {\n                path: { type: \"string\" },\n                content: { type: \"string\" },\n              },\n              required: [\"path\", \"content\"],\n            },\n          },\n        },\n        required: [\"files\"],\n      },\n    },\n  },\n  {\n    type: \"function\",\n    function: {\n      name: \"github_push\",\n      description:\n        \"Push committed work from this workspace's dedicated GitHub branch. \" +\n        \"Use git status/diff/log first, commit with run_command, then call this. \" +\n        \"Never pushes the selected base branch and never force-pushes. Requires user approval.\",\n      parameters: {\n        type: \"object\",\n        properties: {\n          reason: {\n            type: \"string\",\n            description: \"One short line explaining what is ready to publish.\",\n          },\n        },\n        required: [\"reason\"],\n      },\n    },\n  },\n  {\n    type: \"function\",\n    function: {\n      name: \"download_file\",\n      description:\n        \"Save the exact bytes from a URL straight into the workspace — PDFs, \" +\n        \"images, archives, datasets, or text. A downloaded PDF can be passed \" +\n        \"to read_document and an image to view_image. Use this instead of \" +\n        \"asking the user to download something and attach it.\",\n      parameters: {\n        type: \"object\",\n        properties: {\n          url: { type: \"string\", description: \"Full URL, including https://\" },\n          path: {\n            type: \"string\",\n            description: \"Where to save it, relative to the workspace root.\",\n          },\n          allow_local: {\n            type: \"boolean\",\n            description:\n              \"Set true only when downloading from a development server on \" +\n              \"localhost/127.0.0.1/[::1]. Private LAN and metadata addresses remain blocked.\",\n          },\n        },\n        required: [\"url\", \"path\"],\n      },\n    },\n  },\n];\n\nexport interface ToolResult {\n  /** Text handed back to the model as the tool message. */\n  content: string;\n  /** Structured summary for the UI. */\n  summary: string;\n  ok: boolean;\n  /** Files touched, so the UI can refresh its tree. */\n  changedPath?: string;\n}\n\nfunction str(args: Record<string, unknown>, key: string): string {\n  const value = args[key];\n  if (typeof value !== \"string\") {\n    throw new WorkspaceError(`\"${key}\" must be a string`);\n  }\n  return value;\n}\n\n/**\n * An optional numeric argument.\n *\n * Returns null when absent, so \"not given\" and \"given as zero\" stay\n * distinguishable. Models sometimes send numbers as strings, and rejecting\n * \"12\" when 12 was meant costs a whole round to correct.\n */\nfunction num(args: Record<string, unknown>, key: string): number | null {\n  const value = args[key];\n  if (value === undefined || value === null || value === \"\") return null;\n  const parsed = typeof value === \"number\" ? value : Number(value);\n  if (!Number.isFinite(parsed)) return null;\n  return Math.trunc(parsed);\n}\n\n/**\n * Execute one tool call.\n *\n * Errors are returned as tool results rather than thrown: the model needs to\n * see \"that path doesn't exist\" so it can correct itself, and a thrown error\n * would abandon the whole turn instead.\n */\nexport interface ToolContext {\n  /** Vision provider key. Absent means view_image is unavailable. */\n  visionKey?: string;\n  visionModel?: string;\n  /** Tavily key. Absent means web_search is withheld from the model. */\n  searchKey?: string;\n  /** Optional Exa key, used when Tavily refuses. Either one enables search. */\n  exaKey?: string;\n  /** Needed by the search planner, which uses a cheap model to pick queries. */\n  deepseekKey?: string;\n  searchProfile?: string;\n}\n\nexport async function runTool(\n  workspaceId: string,\n  name: string,\n  args: Record<string, unknown>,\n  context: ToolContext = {}\n): Promise<ToolResult> {\n  try {\n    switch (name) {\n      case \"list_files\": {\n        const sub = typeof args.path === \"string\" ? args.path : \".\";\n        const files = await listFiles(workspaceId, sub);\n        if (files.length === 0) {\n          return {\n            ok: true,\n            content: \"The workspace is empty.\",\n            summary: \"Listed files — workspace is empty\",\n          };\n        }\n        const listing = files\n          .map((f) => `${f.path} (${f.size} bytes)`)\n          .join(\"\\n\");\n        return {\n          ok: true,\n          content: `${files.length} file(s):\\n${listing}`,\n          summary: `Listed ${files.length} file${files.length === 1 ? \"\" : \"s\"}`,\n        };\n      }\n\n      case \"read_file\": {\n        const result = await readFile(workspaceId, str(args, \"path\"));\n        const note = result.truncated\n          ? \"\\n\\n[truncated — file is larger than the read limit]\"\n          : \"\";\n\n        /*\n         * Optional line range.\n         *\n         * The parameters were accepted by callers and silently ignored: asking\n         * for lines 1-2 of an eight-line file returned all eight. Harmless on\n         * a small file, expensive on a large one — reading a 3000-line module\n         * to change one function is most of a round's budget spent on context\n         * that is never used.\n         */\n        const total = result.content.split(\"\\n\").length;\n        const start = num(args, \"start_line\");\n        const end = num(args, \"end_line\");\n\n        if (start === null && end === null) {\n          return {\n            ok: true,\n            content: `${result.path}:\\n\\n${result.content}${note}`,\n            summary: `Read ${result.path}`,\n          };\n        }\n\n        const from = Math.max(1, start ?? 1);\n        const to = Math.min(total, end ?? total);\n        if (from > total) {\n          return {\n            ok: false,\n            content:\n              `Error: ${result.path} has ${total} lines, so line ${from} ` +\n              `does not exist.`,\n            summary: `Line ${from} is past the end of ${result.path}`,\n          };\n        }\n\n        const slice = result.content.split(\"\\n\").slice(from - 1, to);\n        /*\n         * Numbered, because a slice without them is a trap.\n         *\n         * Handed lines 400-460 as bare text, a model reasons about them as if\n         * they were the file — reporting \"the bug is on line 12\" when it means\n         * line 411. The numbers cost a few tokens and make the offset\n         * impossible to lose.\n         */\n        const width = String(to).length;\n        const numbered = slice\n          .map((line, i) => `${String(from + i).padStart(width)} | ${line}`)\n          .join(\"\\n\");\n\n        return {\n          ok: true,\n          content:\n            `${result.path} (lines ${from}-${to} of ${total}):\\n\\n` +\n            `${numbered}${note}`,\n          summary: `Read ${result.path} lines ${from}-${to}`,\n        };\n      }\n\n      case \"read_files\": {\n        const raw = Array.isArray(args.paths) ? args.paths : [];\n        if (raw.length === 0) {\n          return {\n            ok: false,\n            content: \"Error: paths must be a non-empty list of file paths.\",\n            summary: \"No paths given\",\n          };\n        }\n\n        // Capped so one call can't pull the whole workspace into context.\n        //\n        // Was 10, which is fewer files than a small project has. Asked to\n        // describe a whole codebase the model would request thirty paths in\n        // one call, twenty were dropped with a note it did not always act\n        // on, and the answer covered a third of the project. The cap exists\n        // to stop a runaway call, not to ration ordinary reading, so it is\n        // set where a real request will not hit it.\n        const paths = raw.slice(0, MAX_READ_FILES).map((p) => String(p));\n        const parts: string[] = [];\n        let read = 0;\n\n        // Read together, reported in the order asked for. Sixty local files\n        // is only a few milliseconds either way, but the ordering guarantee\n        // matters: the model refers to them by position in its own request.\n        const results = await Promise.all(\n          paths.map((filePath) =>\n            readFile(workspaceId, filePath)\n              .then((result) => ({ filePath, result, error: null as unknown }))\n              .catch((error: unknown) => ({ filePath, result: null, error }))\n          )\n        );\n\n        for (const entry of results) {\n          if (entry.result) {\n            read++;\n            const note = entry.result.truncated\n              ? \"\\n\\n[truncated — file is larger than the read limit]\"\n              : \"\";\n            parts.push(\n              `--- ${entry.result.path} ---\\n${entry.result.content}${note}`\n            );\n          } else {\n            // One missing file must not lose the others: report it inline and\n            // keep going, so the model still gets what does exist.\n            parts.push(\n              `--- ${entry.filePath} ---\\n[could not read: ${\n                entry.error instanceof WorkspaceError\n                  ? entry.error.message\n                  : \"unreadable\"\n              }]`\n            );\n          }\n        }\n\n        if (raw.length > paths.length) {\n          // Named explicitly, with an instruction. A bare \"ignored\" note was\n          // treated as commentary: the model carried on and answered as if it\n          // had read everything, so files silently missing from the answer\n          // looked like the agent giving up early.\n          const dropped = raw.slice(paths.length).map((p) => String(p));\n          parts.push(\n            `[NOT READ — ${dropped.length} path(s) exceeded the ${MAX_READ_FILES}-per-call limit: ` +\n              `${dropped.join(\", \")}. ` +\n              `Call read_files again with these before you answer. Do not ` +\n              `describe them as if you had read them.]`\n          );\n        }\n\n        return {\n          ok: read > 0,\n          content: parts.join(\"\\n\\n\"),\n          summary:\n            read === paths.length\n              ? `Read ${read} file${read === 1 ? \"\" : \"s\"}`\n              : `Read ${read} of ${paths.length} files`,\n        };\n      }\n\n      case \"search_files\": {\n        const result = await searchFiles(workspaceId, str(args, \"query\"), {\n          regex: args.regex === true,\n          caseSensitive: args.case_sensitive === true,\n          glob: typeof args.glob === \"string\" ? args.glob : undefined,\n          context: num(args, \"context\") ?? 0,\n        });\n\n        if (result.hits.length === 0) {\n          return {\n            ok: true,\n            content:\n              `No matches in ${result.filesSearched} file` +\n              `${result.filesSearched === 1 ? \"\" : \"s\"}.`,\n            summary: \"No matches\",\n          };\n        }\n\n        const lines = result.hits.map((h) => {\n          if (!h.before?.length && !h.after?.length) {\n            return `${h.path}:${h.line}: ${h.text}`;\n          }\n          // With context, the hit is marked so the model can tell which line\n          // actually matched — otherwise it reasons about a neighbour.\n          const out: string[] = [`${h.path}:${h.line}:`];\n          const first = h.line - (h.before?.length ?? 0);\n          h.before?.forEach((l, i) =>\n            out.push(`  ${String(first + i).padStart(5)}   ${l}`)\n          );\n          out.push(`> ${String(h.line).padStart(5)}   ${h.text}`);\n          h.after?.forEach((l, i) =>\n            out.push(`  ${String(h.line + 1 + i).padStart(5)}   ${l}`)\n          );\n          return out.join(\"\\n\");\n        });\n        if (result.truncated) {\n          lines.push(\"… more matches exist; narrow the search to see them.\");\n        }\n\n        return {\n          ok: true,\n          content: lines.join(\"\\n\"),\n          summary: `${result.hits.length} match${\n            result.hits.length === 1 ? \"\" : \"es\"\n          }`,\n        };\n      }\n\n      case \"start_process\": {\n        const result = await startProcess(\n          workspaceId,\n          str(args, \"command\"),\n          Array.isArray(args.args) ? args.args.map((a) => String(a)) : []\n        );\n\n        if (!result.ok) {\n          return {\n            ok: false,\n            content: `Error: ${result.reason}`,\n            summary: \"Could not start process\",\n          };\n        }\n\n        const { process: proc, diedImmediately } = result;\n        const log = proc.log.trim();\n\n        if (diedImmediately) {\n          // Reported as a failure on purpose: \"started successfully\" for\n          // something already dead would send the model off building on a\n          // false premise.\n          return {\n            ok: false,\n            content:\n              `${proc.display} exited immediately (code ${proc.exitCode ?? \"unknown\"}).\\n\\n` +\n              `${log || \"(no output)\"}\\n\\n` +\n              `Fix the cause before trying again.`,\n            summary: `Failed to start: ${proc.display}`,\n          };\n        }\n\n        return {\n          ok: true,\n          content:\n            `Started ${proc.display} — id ${proc.id}, still running.\\n\\n` +\n            `${log || \"(no output yet)\"}\\n\\n` +\n            `Read more with read_process, and stop it with stop_process when done.`,\n          summary: `Started ${proc.display}`,\n        };\n      }\n\n      case \"read_process\": {\n        const id = typeof args.id === \"string\" ? args.id.trim() : \"\";\n\n        if (!id) {\n          const all = listProcesses(workspaceId);\n          if (all.length === 0) {\n            return {\n              ok: true,\n              content: \"No background processes in this workspace.\",\n              summary: \"No processes\",\n            };\n          }\n          return {\n            ok: true,\n            content: all.map(describeProcess).join(\"\\n\"),\n            summary: `${all.length} process${all.length === 1 ? \"\" : \"es\"}`,\n          };\n        }\n\n        const proc = getProcess(id);\n        // Scoped to the workspace, so one chat cannot read another's output.\n        if (!proc || proc.workspaceId !== workspaceId) {\n          return {\n            ok: false,\n            content: `No process with id \"${id}\" in this workspace.`,\n            summary: \"Unknown process\",\n          };\n        }\n\n        const note = proc.truncated\n          ? \"\\n\\n[earlier output dropped — only the most recent is kept]\"\n          : \"\";\n\n        /*\n         * Only the last N lines, when asked for.\n         *\n         * Polling a dev server meant re-reading its entire log every time,\n         * and that whole log then rode along in the transcript on every later\n         * round. On a watcher that prints a line a second, the interesting\n         * part is always the end — and `tail` makes checking twice cost\n         * almost nothing instead of doubling the context.\n         */\n        const tailLines = num(args, \"tail\");\n        let body = proc.log.trim() || \"(no output)\";\n        let trimmedNote = \"\";\n        if (tailLines && tailLines > 0) {\n          const lines = body.split(\"\\n\");\n          if (lines.length > tailLines) {\n            trimmedNote =\n              `\\n\\n[showing the last ${tailLines} of ${lines.length} lines]`;\n            body = lines.slice(-tailLines).join(\"\\n\");\n          }\n        }\n\n        return {\n          ok: true,\n          content:\n            `${describeProcess(proc)}\\n\\n${body}${trimmedNote}${note}`,\n          summary: isRunning(proc)\n            ? `Read ${proc.display}`\n            : `${proc.display} has stopped`,\n        };\n      }\n\n      case \"write_process\": {\n        const id = str(args, \"id\").trim();\n        const input = typeof args.input === \"string\" ? args.input : \"\";\n\n        const proc = getProcess(id);\n        // Workspace-scoped like every other process call: one chat must not\n        // be able to type into another chat's process.\n        if (!proc || proc.workspaceId !== workspaceId) {\n          return {\n            ok: false,\n            content: `No process with id \"${id}\" in this workspace. Use read_process with no id to list them.`,\n            summary: \"Unknown process\",\n          };\n        }\n\n        const res = writeToProcess(id, input);\n        if (!res.ok) {\n          return {\n            ok: false,\n            content: `Could not send that: ${res.reason}`,\n            summary: \"Write failed\",\n          };\n        }\n\n        /*\n         * A short pause, then the new output.\n         *\n         * Sending input and returning immediately shows the log as it was\n         * BEFORE the process reacted, which reads as \"nothing happened\" and\n         * invites the model to send it again. 250ms is enough for a prompt\n         * to advance without being a wait the user notices.\n         */\n        await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 250));\n        const after = getProcess(id);\n        const tail = (after?.log ?? \"\").split(\"\\n\").slice(-15).join(\"\\n\");\n\n        return {\n          ok: true,\n          content:\n            `Sent to ${proc.display}: ${input.trim()}\\n\\n` +\n            `Output since (last 15 lines):\\n${tail || \"(nothing yet)\"}\\n\\n` +\n            `Read it again with read_process if it needed longer to respond.`,\n          summary: `Sent \"${input.trim().slice(0, 20)}\"`,\n        };\n      }\n\n      case \"stop_process\": {\n        const id = str(args, \"id\").trim();\n\n        if (id === \"all\") {\n          const stopped = stopAll(workspaceId);\n          return {\n            ok: true,\n            content:\n              stopped === 0\n                ? \"Nothing was running.\"\n                : `Stopped ${stopped} process${stopped === 1 ? \"\" : \"es\"}.`,\n            summary: `Stopped ${stopped}`,\n          };\n        }\n\n        const proc = getProcess(id);\n        if (!proc || proc.workspaceId !== workspaceId) {\n          return {\n            ok: false,\n            content: `No process with id \"${id}\" in this workspace.`,\n            summary: \"Unknown process\",\n          };\n        }\n\n        stopProcess(id);\n        return {\n          ok: true,\n          content: `Stopped ${proc.display}.`,\n          summary: `Stopped ${proc.display}`,\n        };\n      }\n\n      case \"view_image\": {\n        if (!context.visionKey) {\n          // Reported as a tool result rather than an error, so the model can\n          // tell the user what to do instead of retrying forever.\n          return {\n            ok: false,\n            content:\n              \"No vision key is configured, so images cannot be viewed. \" +\n              \"Tell the user to add one in Settings.\",\n            summary: \"Vision not configured\",\n          };\n        }\n\n        const imagePath = str(args, \"path\");\n        const image = await readImageAsDataUrl(workspaceId, imagePath);\n\n        const result = await describeImage(\n          image.dataUrl,\n          context.visionKey,\n          context.visionModel,\n          typeof args.question === \"string\" ? args.question : undefined\n        );\n\n        if (result.error) {\n          return {\n            ok: false,\n            content: `Could not read ${imagePath}: ${result.error}`,\n            summary: `Couldn't view ${imagePath}`,\n          };\n        }\n\n        return {\n          ok: true,\n          content: `${imagePath}:\\n\\n${result.description ?? \"(no description)\"}`,\n          summary: `Viewed ${imagePath}`,\n        };\n      }\n\n      case \"write_file\": {\n        const result = await writeFile(\n          workspaceId,\n          str(args, \"path\"),\n          str(args, \"content\")\n        );\n        return {\n          ok: true,\n          content: `${result.created ? \"Created\" : \"Updated\"} ${result.path} (${result.bytes} bytes).`,\n          summary: `${result.created ? \"Created\" : \"Updated\"} ${result.path}`,\n          changedPath: result.path,\n        };\n      }\n\n      case \"edit_file\": {\n        const filePath = str(args, \"path\");\n\n        // Captured before the edit so the result can show what actually\n        // changed. Without it the model is told only \"Edited main.py\" and\n        // cannot tell a correct edit from one that landed in the wrong place.\n        let before: string | null = null;\n        try {\n          before = (await readFile(workspaceId, filePath)).content;\n        } catch {\n          before = null;\n        }\n\n        const result = await editFile(\n          workspaceId,\n          filePath,\n          str(args, \"old_text\"),\n          str(args, \"new_text\")\n        );\n\n        let confirmation = `Edited ${result.path}.`;\n        if (before !== null) {\n          try {\n            const after = (await readFile(workspaceId, filePath)).content;\n            const changed = diffLines(before, after);\n            const stats = diffStats(changed);\n            const hunks = diffHunks(changed, 2);\n\n            // Show the surrounding lines, so the model can see whether the\n            // replacement sits where it intended rather than assuming it does.\n            const preview = hunks\n              .flatMap((h) => h.lines)\n              .slice(0, 40)\n              .map((l) =>\n                `${l.kind === \"added\" ? \"+\" : l.kind === \"removed\" ? \"-\" : \" \"} ${l.text}`\n              )\n              .join(\"\\n\");\n\n            confirmation =\n              `Edited ${result.path} (+${stats.added} -${stats.removed}).\\n\\n` +\n              `${preview}\\n\\n` +\n              `Check this is the change you intended before moving on.`;\n          } catch {\n            /* fall back to the plain confirmation */\n          }\n        }\n\n        return {\n          ok: true,\n          content: confirmation,\n          summary: `Edited ${result.path}`,\n          changedPath: result.path,\n        };\n      }\n\n      case \"delete_file\": {\n        const result = await deleteFile(workspaceId, str(args, \"path\"));\n        return {\n          ok: true,\n          content: `Deleted ${result.path}.`,\n          summary: `Deleted ${result.path}`,\n          changedPath: result.path,\n        };\n      }\n\n      case \"fetch_url\": {\n        const wantsRaw = args.raw === true;\n        const page = await fetchPage(str(args, \"url\"), { raw: wantsRaw });\n\n        const header = [\n          `${page.url}`,\n          page.title ? `Title: ${page.title}` : null,\n          `HTTP ${page.status} · ${page.contentType} · ${(page.bytes / 1024).toFixed(0)}KB`,\n          page.truncated\n            ? `[truncated at ${MAX_FETCH_CHARS.toLocaleString()} characters]`\n            : null,\n        ]\n          .filter(Boolean)\n          .join(\"\\n\");\n\n        let body = wantsRaw && page.html ? page.html : page.text;\n\n        /*\n         * Narrowing, because the whole page is often the wrong amount.\n         *\n         * Reported from a real test: fetching PyPI's JSON to read one version\n         * string returned 477KB, truncated at 200,000 characters — the answer\n         * was in there, but so was the release history of every version since\n         * 2021, and a truncated body can cut off the very line that was\n         * wanted.\n         *\n         * A literal substring is tried as a regex first, so both work. An\n         * invalid pattern falls back to a literal search rather than failing:\n         * a model writing `info.version` means the text, not a character\n         * class.\n         */\n        const find = typeof args.find === \"string\" ? args.find.trim() : \"\";\n        let findNote = \"\";\n        if (find) {\n          /*\n           * Match on CHARACTER OFFSETS, not on lines.\n           *\n           * The first version split the body into lines and kept the matching\n           * ones with two either side. That works on pretty-printed text and\n           * does nothing at all on minified JSON — which is most API\n           * responses. Reported from a real test against PyPI: the whole\n           * 477KB document is ONE line, so \"the matching line\" was the entire\n           * file and `find` filtered one line down to one line.\n           *\n           * Windowing around each match instead works on both shapes: a line\n           * in pretty-printed JSON is well under the window, and a minified\n           * blob gets a slice around the needle rather than the ocean.\n           */\n          const WINDOW = 300;\n          const MAX_MATCHES = 20;\n\n          let re: RegExp;\n          try {\n            re = new RegExp(find, \"gi\");\n          } catch {\n            // A model writing \"info.version[\" means the text, not a broken\n            // character class.\n            re = new RegExp(find.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\\]\\\\]/g, \"\\\\$&\"), \"gi\");\n          }\n\n          const spans: [number, number][] = [];\n          for (const m of body.matchAll(re)) {\n            if (m.index === undefined) continue;\n            spans.push([\n              Math.max(0, m.index - WINDOW),\n              Math.min(body.length, m.index + m[0].length + WINDOW),\n            ]);\n            if (spans.length >= MAX_MATCHES) break;\n          }\n\n          if (spans.length === 0) {\n            findNote =\n              `\\n\\n[Nothing matched \"${find}\". The page is ` +\n              `${body.length.toLocaleString()} characters — fetch it again ` +\n              `without find, or try a different pattern.]`;\n            body = \"\";\n          } else {\n            // Overlapping windows are merged so a dense cluster of matches\n            // reads as one passage rather than the same text repeated.\n            const merged: [number, number][] = [];\n            for (const [from, to] of spans) {\n              const last = merged[merged.length - 1];\n              if (last && from <= last[1]) last[1] = Math.max(last[1], to);\n              else merged.push([from, to]);\n            }\n\n            const pieces = merged.map(([from, to]) => {\n              const lead = from > 0 ? \"…\" : \"\";\n              const trail = to < body.length ? \"…\" : \"\";\n              return `${lead}${body.slice(from, to)}${trail}`;\n            });\n\n            const shown = pieces.join(\"\\n\\n\");\n            findNote =\n              `\\n[Showing ${merged.length} match${merged.length === 1 ? \"\" : \"es\"} ` +\n              `for \"${find}\" with ${WINDOW} characters of context each, out of ` +\n              `${body.length.toLocaleString()} characters.` +\n              `${spans.length >= MAX_MATCHES ? ` Stopped at ${MAX_MATCHES} matches.` : \"\"}]`;\n            body = shown.slice(0, MAX_FETCH_CHARS);\n          }\n        }\n\n        /*\n         * Say so when this tool is the wrong one.\n         *\n         * An app shell fetches successfully and contains nothing. Reporting\n         * that as a normal result is how the model ends up writing selectors\n         * for a DOM that was never sent — it had no way to tell the page was\n         * empty rather than simply short.\n         */\n        const warning = page.needsBrowser\n          ? `\\n\\n[This page is an app shell — its content is built by ` +\n            `JavaScript, which has not run here, so the text and markup above ` +\n            `are nearly empty. Use browse for this URL instead: it runs the ` +\n            `scripts and returns the real DOM. Do not write selectors from ` +\n            `what you see above.]`\n          : \"\";\n\n        return {\n          ok: true,\n          content: `${header}${warning}${findNote}\\n\\n${body}`,\n          summary: page.needsBrowser\n            ? `${new URL(page.url).hostname} needs a browser`\n            : `Read ${new URL(page.url).hostname}${\n                page.title ? ` — ${page.title.slice(0, 50)}` : \"\"\n              }`,\n        };\n      }\n\n      case \"inspect_page\": {\n        const page = await fetchPage(str(args, \"url\"), { raw: true });\n        if (!page.html) {\n          return {\n            ok: false,\n            content:\n              `${page.url} returned ${page.contentType}, not HTML, so it has ` +\n              `no selectors to inspect.`,\n            summary: \"Not an HTML page\",\n          };\n        }\n\n        if (page.needsBrowser) {\n          // Refused rather than answered. inspect_page exists to hand back\n          // selectors, and returning `id=root` as though it were the page's\n          // structure is precisely the failure this whole area was fixed for.\n          return {\n            ok: false,\n            content:\n              `${page.url} is an app shell: the markup the server sent ` +\n              `contains no real content, because the page is built by ` +\n              `JavaScript that has not run. Any selector taken from it would ` +\n              `not exist in the live page.\\n\\nUse browse on this URL — it ` +\n              `runs the scripts and returns the rendered DOM.`,\n            summary: \"Needs a browser, not a fetch\",\n          };\n        }\n\n        const found = extractSelectors(page.html);\n        const filter =\n          typeof args.contains === \"string\" ? args.contains.toLowerCase() : \"\";\n        const keep = (list: string[]) =>\n          filter ? list.filter((v) => v.toLowerCase().includes(filter)) : list;\n\n        const ids = keep(found.ids);\n        const classes = keep(found.classes);\n        const attrs = keep(found.dataAttrs);\n\n        if (ids.length === 0 && classes.length === 0 && attrs.length === 0) {\n          return {\n            ok: true,\n            content: filter\n              ? `No ids, classes or data-attributes on ${page.url} contain \"${filter}\". ` +\n                `The page has ${found.ids.length} ids and ${found.classes.length} ` +\n                `classes in total — try a different word, or call again without a filter.`\n              : `${page.url} has no ids, classes or data attributes to list. ` +\n                `That is valid for a simple static page built from plain tags; ` +\n                `there is no evidence here that JavaScript is involved. Read ` +\n                `the raw HTML with fetch_url if tag structure is enough, or ` +\n                `inspect a more specific page.`,\n            summary: \"No selectors found\",\n          };\n        }\n\n        const section = (label: string, list: string[]) =>\n          list.length ? `${label} (${list.length}):\\n${list.join(\"\\n\")}` : null;\n\n        return {\n          ok: true,\n          content: [\n            `Selectors on ${page.url}${filter ? ` matching \"${filter}\"` : \"\"}:`,\n            \"\",\n            section(\"IDs\", ids),\n            section(\"Classes\", classes),\n            section(\"Data attributes\", attrs),\n            \"\",\n            \"These are the real names on the page. Target these exactly rather \" +\n              \"than inventing selectors.\",\n          ]\n            .filter(Boolean)\n            .join(\"\\n\"),\n          summary: `Inspected ${new URL(page.url).hostname} — ${\n            ids.length + classes.length\n          } selectors`,\n        };\n      }\n\n      case \"download_file\": {\n        const target = str(args, \"path\");\n        const resource = await downloadResource(str(args, \"url\"), {\n          allowLocal: args.allow_local === true,\n        });\n        // Bytes, never decoded text. This is what lets a downloaded PDF flow\n        // directly into read_document and an image into view_image without\n        // being corrupted or refused as \"not a page\".\n        const written = await writeFileBytes(\n          workspaceId,\n          target,\n          Buffer.from(resource.data)\n        );\n\n        return {\n          ok: true,\n          content:\n            `Saved ${resource.url} to ${written.path} (${written.bytes} bytes, ` +\n            `${resource.contentType}).`,\n          summary: `Downloaded ${written.path}`,\n          changedPath: written.path,\n        };\n      }\n\n      case \"move_file\": {\n        const result = await moveFile(\n          workspaceId,\n          str(args, \"from\"),\n          str(args, \"to\")\n        );\n        return {\n          ok: true,\n          content: `Moved ${result.from} to ${result.to} (${result.bytes} bytes).`,\n          summary: `Moved ${result.from} → ${result.to}`,\n          changedPath: result.to,\n        };\n      }\n\n      case \"edit_files\": {\n        const raw = Array.isArray(args.edits) ? args.edits : [];\n        if (raw.length === 0) {\n          return {\n            ok: false,\n            content: \"Error: edits must be a non-empty list.\",\n            summary: \"No edits given\",\n          };\n        }\n\n        const batch = raw.slice(0, MAX_BATCH_EDITS);\n        const done: string[] = [];\n        const failed: string[] = [];\n\n        for (const entry of batch) {\n          const edit = entry as {\n            path?: unknown;\n            old_text?: unknown;\n            new_text?: unknown;\n          };\n          if (\n            typeof edit.path !== \"string\" ||\n            typeof edit.old_text !== \"string\" ||\n            typeof edit.new_text !== \"string\"\n          ) {\n            failed.push(`${String(edit.path ?? \"?\")} — malformed edit`);\n            continue;\n          }\n          try {\n            const result = await editFile(\n              workspaceId,\n              edit.path,\n              edit.old_text,\n              edit.new_text\n            );\n            done.push(result.path);\n          } catch (error) {\n            /*\n             * One failure does not abandon the rest.\n             *\n             * Half-applying a refactor sounds worse than applying none of it,\n             * but the alternative is silently reverting edits that were\n             * correct — and the model cannot tell which those were. Naming\n             * exactly what failed lets it fix that one and move on.\n             */\n            failed.push(\n              `${edit.path} — ${\n                error instanceof WorkspaceError ? error.message : \"could not be edited\"\n              }`\n            );\n          }\n        }\n\n        /*\n         * Count files, not edits.\n         *\n         * `done` holds one entry per successful EDIT, and several edits to the\n         * same file is the normal case — two bugs in one file is two entries.\n         * Reporting that as \"Edited 2 file(s)\" is wrong in the one direction\n         * that matters: it tells the model it touched more of the workspace\n         * than it did.\n         *\n         * Seen in a real run: the model fixed both bugs in counter.py with one\n         * edit_files call and was told it had edited two files. The work was\n         * correct; the receipt was not.\n         */\n        const distinct = [...new Set(done)];\n        const fileWord = (n: number) => `${n} file${n === 1 ? \"\" : \"s\"}`;\n\n        const notes: string[] = [];\n        if (done.length) {\n          notes.push(\n            `Applied ${done.length} edit${done.length === 1 ? \"\" : \"s\"} to ` +\n              `${fileWord(distinct.length)}:\\n${distinct.join(\"\\n\")}`\n          );\n        }\n        if (failed.length) {\n          notes.push(\n            `Failed ${failed.length} — these were NOT applied, fix and retry ` +\n              `just these:\\n${failed.join(\"\\n\")}`\n          );\n        }\n        if (raw.length > batch.length) {\n          notes.push(\n            `[${raw.length - batch.length} more ignored — limit is ` +\n              `${MAX_BATCH_EDITS} per call.]`\n          );\n        }\n\n        return {\n          ok: done.length > 0,\n          content: notes.join(\"\\n\\n\"),\n          summary:\n            failed.length === 0\n              ? `Edited ${fileWord(distinct.length)}`\n              : `Edited ${fileWord(distinct.length)}, ${failed.length} failed`,\n          changedPath: done[0],\n        };\n      }\n\n      case \"replace_in_files\": {\n        const find = str(args, \"find\");\n        const replace = str(args, \"replace\");\n        if (!find) {\n          return {\n            ok: false,\n            content: \"Error: find must not be empty.\",\n            summary: \"Empty search\",\n          };\n        }\n\n        const preview = args.preview === true;\n        const glob = typeof args.glob === \"string\" ? args.glob : undefined;\n        const useRegex = args.regex === true;\n\n        /*\n         * Regex, because exact-match is the most common self-inflicted\n         * failure.\n         *\n         * Reported: \"one drifted space or shifted line and the edit dies\".\n         * edit_file already tolerates whitespace across three passes, but\n         * replace_in_files was strictly literal — so a rename where the\n         * surrounding text varies had no tool at all, and the fallback was\n         * one edit per file.\n         *\n         * searchFiles already understood regex; this simply stopped throwing\n         * that away. Validated here rather than at match time so a bad\n         * pattern is a clear error instead of a silent zero-match.\n         */\n        let pattern: RegExp | null = null;\n        if (useRegex) {\n          try {\n            pattern = new RegExp(find, \"g\");\n          } catch (error) {\n            return {\n              ok: false,\n              content:\n                `Error: \"${find}\" is not a valid regular expression — ` +\n                `${error instanceof Error ? error.message : \"could not be parsed\"}. ` +\n                `Fix the pattern, or drop regex to search for it literally.`,\n              summary: \"Bad pattern\",\n            };\n          }\n        }\n\n        // Reuses the same matcher the search tool uses, so a preview and the\n        // real thing can never disagree about which files are in scope.\n        const hits = await searchFiles(workspaceId, find, {\n          glob,\n          regex: useRegex,\n        });\n        const paths = [...new Set(hits.hits.map((h) => h.path))];\n\n        if (paths.length === 0) {\n          return {\n            ok: false,\n            content:\n              `\"${find}\" does not appear in any file${glob ? ` matching ${glob}` : \"\"}. ` +\n              `Check the exact text, or search first.`,\n            summary: \"No matches\",\n          };\n        }\n\n        const changed: string[] = [];\n        const failed: string[] = [];\n        let occurrences = 0;\n\n        for (const filePath of paths) {\n          try {\n            const file = await readFile(workspaceId, filePath);\n\n            let count: number;\n            let updated: string;\n            if (pattern) {\n              // A fresh lastIndex per file: a /g regex is stateful, and\n              // reusing one across files silently skips matches.\n              const re = new RegExp(pattern.source, pattern.flags);\n              count = [...file.content.matchAll(re)].length;\n              updated = file.content.replace(\n                new RegExp(pattern.source, pattern.flags),\n                replace\n              );\n            } else {\n              count = file.content.split(find).length - 1;\n              updated = file.content.split(find).join(replace);\n            }\n            if (count === 0) continue;\n\n            occurrences += count;\n            if (!preview) {\n              await writeFile(workspaceId, filePath, updated);\n            }\n            changed.push(`${filePath} (${count})`);\n          } catch (error) {\n            failed.push(\n              `${filePath} — ${\n                error instanceof WorkspaceError ? error.message : \"could not be updated\"\n              }`\n            );\n          }\n        }\n\n        const heading = preview\n          ? `Would replace ${occurrences} occurrence(s) of \"${find}\" across ${changed.length} file(s). [STEP-START] {"type":"step-start"}
I’m building this in layers so “deep” does not make ordinary use slow:

1. **Always-available built-in PE analysis**—no external tools and no execution.
2. **Recursive local DLL graph** with imported function names, including delay-loaded and likely runtime-loaded DLLs.
3. **Managed/.NET decompilation** through ILSpy when available.
4. **Native C-like decompilation** through headless Ghidra when available.
5. **Hash-based caching and hard process/time/output caps**, so the expensive layer runs once per binary rather than on every question.

The target executable will never be launched. Packed/encrypted binaries cannot always be fully reconstructed, so the tool will report exactly what was statically recovered and what prevented deeper output.

Yes—implemented and pushed.

## What it can now read

New first-class tool:

```text
inspect_binary
```

Supported uploads:

```text
.exe .dll .sys .ocx .scr .cpl .drv .efi
```

It can also preserve executables found inside selected folders, ZIP, TAR, and TAR.GZ archives.

### Built-in analysis, requiring no setup

- PE32 and PE32+ parsing
- x86, x64, ARM64 and other machine types
- SHA-256, SHA-1, MD5 and imphash
- Entry point, image base, subsystem and mapped size
- Sections, permissions and entropy
- Normal and delay-loaded DLL imports
- Exact imported function names and ordinals
- Exports and forwarded exports
- Recursive local DLL dependency graph
- .NET assembly identity and referenced assemblies
- PDB/debug paths
- Version information
- ASCII and UTF-16 strings
- Possible runtime-loaded DLLs
- ASLR, DEP and CFG status
- Authenticode envelope presence—without falsely claiming trust verification
- Overlay/appended payload detection
- Structural observations such as RWX sections and high entropy

The executable is **never launched**.

## Deep decompilation

### Managed .NET executables

Uses ILSpy to generate C#-like source and project files:

```bat
dotnet tool install --global ilspycmd
```

### Native executables

Uses headless Ghidra to generate indexed, searchable C-like pseudocode in approximately 350 KB chunks.

Install Ghidra and Java 21, then add this to `.env.local`:

```env
APIM_GHIDRA_HOME=C:\Tools\ghidra_11.x_PUBLIC
```

That folder must contain:

```text
support\analyzeHeadless.bat
```

Restart apiM after configuring it.

Deep analysis defaults:

```env
APIM_BINARY_DECOMPILE_TIMEOUT_MS=240000
APIM_BINARY_MAX_CPU=4
APIM_BINARY_MAX_OUTPUT_MB=100
```

Results are cached by SHA-256. Pressing Stop kills the complete Ghidra/ILSpy process tree; the regression test stopped a fake heavy decompiler in approximately **100 ms**.

Packed, encrypted, obfuscated, or heavily optimized executables may only produce partial pseudocode. Exact original variable names, comments and source structure cannot generally be recovered.

- Binary suite: **41/41**
- Complete audit: **1,862/1,862 across 47 suites**
- TypeScript: passed
- ESLint: passed
- Production build: passed
- `inspect_binary` tool score: **96.7%**
- Real ILSpy/Ghidra decompilation was not run in Arena because neither external program is installed here.

- **Arena sandbox right now:** no `capa`, no `ilspycmd`, no Ghidra `analyzeHeadless`, no Java, no .NET SDK.

## Coverage: before vs now

| Requested capability | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Full strings dump | Only 160 ranked strings | **Complete ASCII + both-alignment UTF-16LE dumps**, with offsets, lengths and encoding |
| 2. PE summary | Mostly available | **Full JSON summary** with sections, sizes, timestamp and explicit packing likelihood/score/reasons |
| 3. Entropy map | Per-section only | **4KB-window entropy map** with file offsets and section names |
| 4. Carved blobs | Missing | **PE/DLL, Lua bytecode/source, ZIP, PNG and PDF carving**, each with its own strings dump |
| 5. Interesting imports | Generic imports only | Dedicated grouping for `luaL_*`, `CreateRemoteThread`, `WriteProcessMemory`, `LoadLibrary*`, `GetProcAddress`, `CreateProcess*`, and related APIs |
| 6. capa report | Missing | **FLARE capa integration**, cached with explicit installed/unavailable/failed status |
| 7. Focused decompilation | Full broad decompile only | **Ghidra/ILSpy focused-only output for `CreateMove` and `IN_JUMP` by default** |

Artifacts are stored under:

```text
analysis/<binary>-<sha256-prefix>/
├── static/
│   ├── pe-summary.json
│   ├── entropy-map-0001.tsv
│   ├── strings/
│   │   ├── full-strings-ascii-0001.tsv
│   │   └── full-strings-utf16le-0001.tsv
│   └── carved/
│       ├── index.json
│       ├── blob-*.dll/.exe/.lua/.luac/.zip/.png/.pdf
│       └── strings/
├── capa/
│   └── capa-report.txt
├── ghidra/
│   ├── focused-functions.c
│   └── focused-functions.tsv
└── ilspy/
    └── focused-functions.cs
```

Files are chunked below the app’s searchable-file ceiling, so the agent can use `search_files` on full strings and entropy results.

## Focused decompilation behavior

Default focus:

```json
{
  "focus_terms": ["CreateMove", "IN_JUMP"],
  "focused_only": true
}
```

Ghidra resolves:

- Matching function names
- Matching symbol names
- References to matching symbols
- References to matching data strings

ILSpy extracts matching C# method blocks and removes the full project in focused-only mode.

To retain complete decompilation as well:

```json
{
  "focused_only": false
}
```

Important limitation: `IN_JUMP` may be a compile-time constant whose name disappeared during compilation. If no symbol, PDB information, string, or recoverable decompiler reference remains, no static tool can recreate that original macro name. The report says zero matches instead of inventing one.

USER:
you said that some of them are optional optional you mean that it depends on app or do i need to enable it?

ARENA:
[STEP-START] {"type":"step-start"}
“Optional” means **apiM works without those external programs**, but deeper analysis becomes available when you install them.

You do **not** need to enable a UI toggle. `inspect_binary` attempts static artifacts, capa, and deep decompilation by default, then automatically detects what is installed.

## Always available

These work immediately after updating apiM:

- Full strings dump
- PE summary
- Packing assessment
- Entropy map
- Embedded blob carving
- Interesting imports
- Recursive DLL graph
- Basic .NET metadata
- Hashes, sections, exports, PDB paths

No configuration required.

## Optional external programs

| Program | Used for | Required? |
|---|---|---|
| **capa** | Capability/rule report | Optional |
| **ILSpy** | C# decompilation of managed .NET EXEs/DLLs | Optional |
| **Ghidra + Java 21** | Native x86/x64/ARM C-like decompilation | Optional |

You normally need only **one decompiler per binary**:

- .NET executable → ILSpy
- Native executable → Ghidra
- capa is additional analysis for either

## After installing

### capa

```bat
py -m pip install flare-capa
where capa
```

### ILSpy

Requires the .NET SDK:

```bat
dotnet tool install --global ilspycmd
where ilspycmd
```

If `where` finds them, apiM detects them automatically after restarting:

```bat
rmdir /s /q .next
npm run dev
```

No `.env.local` entry is needed when they are on `PATH`.

### Ghidra

Ghidra is not normally added to `PATH`, so configure it:

```env
APIM_GHIDRA_HOME=C:\Tools\ghidra_11.x_PUBLIC
```

The configured directory must contain:

```text
C:\Tools\ghidra_11.x_PUBLIC\support\analyzeHeadless.bat
```

Ghidra also requires Java 21.

## If something is absent

The entire binary analysis does not fail. It reports, for example:

```text
Static artifacts: complete
capa: unavailable
Deep decompilation: unavailable via ghidra
Setup needed: ...
```

So “optional” means **install it only if you want that deeper layer**. Once installed and visible to apiM, it is used automatically.

See here how to change the file encoding in vscode.\nShare ## Comments\nThis step:\n\n```\necho 'extends: [\"spectral:oas\", \"spectral:asyncapi\"]' > .spectral.yaml\n```\n\nencloses the contents in quotes in the generated .spectral.yaml file, which causes the error. Removing the quotes will leave the value as: ```\nextends: [\"spectral:oas\", \"spectral:asyncapi\"]\n```\n\nwhich is then understood by Spectral and eliminates the cause of the error.\n\n**NOTE:** this is one of many possible error causes, rulesets themselves might have other internal issues.\n\nShare\n\nShare a link to this answer\n\nCC BY-SA 4.0 ## 3 Comments\nRedocly has been much nicer in my exp. Yes—this was our setup/integration problem.

### Cause

`pip install flare-capa` installs the capa engine, but intentionally does **not** include:

- Default capa rules
- Library-identification signatures

The official installation documentation confirms that library installations require separate `-r` and `-s` paths [1](https://github.com/mandiant/capa/blob/master/doc/installation.md).

Our code previously called:

```bat
capa -q sample.exe
```

That had two problems:

1. No rules or signatures paths.
2. `-q` suppresses the actual report.

Both are fixed.

## Update apiM

Stop the server, then:

```bat
git pull --ff-only origin arena/01a0025d-apim
git log -1 --oneline
```

Expected:

```text
93bb2b9 fix: support capa library rules and signatures
```

## Install matching rules and signatures

Your capa version is `9.4.0`, so clone matching `v9.4.0` resources:

```bat
cd C:\Users\Marsel\Desktop\apiM

mkdir tools 2>nul

git clone --depth 1 --branch v9.4.0 https://github.com/mandiant/capa-rules.git tools\capa-rules

git clone --depth 1 --branch v9.4.0 https://github.com/mandiant/capa.git tools\capa
```

Verify:

```bat
dir tools\capa-rules
dir tools\capa\sigs
```

apiM automatically detects those exact locations. No `.env.local` changes are necessary.

Test capa manually:

```bat
capa -r tools\capa-rules -s tools\capa\sigs C:\Windows\System32\notepad.exe
```

Then restart apiM:

```bat
rmdir /s /q .next
npm run dev
```

## What the fix now does

apiM automatically passes:

```text
-r tools/capa-rules
-s tools/capa/sigs
```

It also distinguishes:

```text
capa executable missing
capa engine installed but rules missing
capa engine installed but signatures missing
capa analysis failed
capa analysis complete
```

Custom paths remain available:

```env
APIM_CAPA_RULES_PATH=C:\path\to\capa-rules
APIM_CAPA_SIGNATURES_PATH=C:\path\to\capa\sigs
```

That result exposes two distinct mechanisms:

- **Carving:** not a parser failure. Signature carving found the plaintext PNG, but an encrypted/compressed payload has no `MZ`, Lua, ZIP, or other recoverable signature until it is unpacked. We should still preserve the high-entropy section/overlay as an opaque carved blob instead of returning only the decoy.
- **Ghidra:** this is a real bug. Focused-only mode found no surviving `CreateMove`/`IN_JUMP` symbol/string references, selected zero functions, wrote header-only files, and the adapter incorrectly called that “complete.” Old empty output was then hash-cached.

I’m fixing both: invalidate the empty cache, make zero focused candidates fall back to bounded full decompilation, reject zero-function “success,” and carve high-entropy sections/overlays as opaque payload candidates with their own strings.

Your verdict was correct.

## Actual causes

### Carving: partial, not broken

It found the decoy PNG because that had a plaintext PNG signature. The real payload was compressed/encrypted, so it contained no plaintext:

- `MZ`
- Lua bytecode header
- ZIP signature
- PDF signature
- Other known child format

Signature carving cannot reconstruct plaintext that does not exist until runtime unpacking.

I added:

- Carving of high-entropy PE sections as opaque `.bin` files
- Carving of opaque overlays
- Separate full strings dumps for each opaque region
- Explicit wording that the data is compressed/encrypted—not a recovered payload

This preserves the likely payload region for later Ghidra/capa/manual unpacking instead of returning only the decoy.

### Ghidra: real bug

The exact mechanism was:

1. Focused mode searched for surviving `CreateMove`/`IN_JUMP` symbols or strings.
2. A stripped/packed binary contained neither.
3. Ghidra selected zero functions.
4. It wrote header-only TSV/C files.
5. apiM saw `functions.tsv` and incorrectly marked the analysis complete.
6. That empty result was cached by binary hash.

## Ghidra fixes

- Empty Ghidra cache profile invalidated.
- Zero focused candidates now trigger bounded full decompilation.
- Zero decompiled functions can never be marked complete.
- Successful fallback reports exactly why it ran.
- Cache misses delete old generated chunks before rebuilding.
- Stale files can no longer make a new empty run appear non-empty.
- `summary.txt` is parsed to verify the real number of decompiled functions.

Expected new message when names were stripped:

```text
No surviving CreateMove/IN_JUMP references were found,
so bounded full decompilation ran automatically.
```

If Ghidra still produces zero functions:

```text
Ghidra exited successfully but decompiled zero functions.
This is not accepted as a completed analysis.
```

## What to expect afterward

Because `CreateMove` and `IN_JUMP` apparently do not survive as plaintext symbols, the new Ghidra logic should report:

```text
No surviving CreateMove/IN_JUMP references were found,
so bounded full decompilation ran automatically.
```

Ghidra can decompile the unpacker/loader code, but it cannot directly decompile the 6.6 MB ciphertext as code. Recovering that payload’s plaintext would require identifying its runtime decryption/unpacking routine and obtaining the post-decryption memory contents.

USER:
why cant i gitclone exactly here

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ARENA:
[STEP-START] {"type":"step-start"}
You **can put Ghidra inside the apiM folder**, but `git clone` is the wrong installation method.

### Why cloning does not work

```bat
git clone https://github.com/NationalSecurityAgency/ghidra.git
```

downloads Ghidra’s **source code**, not the compiled application. The source checkout does not provide the ready-to-run top-level file apiM needs:

```text
support\analyzeHeadless.bat
```

You would have to build Ghidra with Gradle first. The release ZIP already contains the compiled application.

capa rules worked with `git clone` because they are plain YAML/signature data; Ghidra is a compiled Java application.

## Install Ghidra inside apiM

Run:

```bat
cd C:\Users\Marsel\Desktop\apiM
mkdir tools 2>nul
```

Download the compiled release:

```bat
curl.exe -L "https://github.com/NationalSecurityAgency/ghidra/releases/download/Ghidra_12.1.2_build/ghidra_12.1.2_PUBLIC_20260605.zip" -o "tools\ghidra.zip"
```

Extract it:

```bat
powershell -NoProfile -Command "Expand-Archive -LiteralPath 'tools\ghidra.zip' -DestinationPath 'tools' -Force"
```

Verify:

```bat
dir "tools\ghidra_12.1.2_PUBLIC\support\analyzeHeadless.bat"
```

Prevent the 570 MB installation from appearing in Git status:

```bat
echo tools/ghidra.zip>>.git/info/exclude
echo tools/ghidra_12.1.2_PUBLIC/>>.git/info/exclude
```

Then add this to `.env.local`:

```env
APIM_GHIDRA_HOME=C:\Users\Marsel\Desktop\apiM\tools\ghidra_12.1.2_PUBLIC
```

Restart:

```bat
rmdir /s /q .next
npm run dev
```

So yes, Ghidra can live “exactly here” under `apiM\tools`; it just needs the compiled release ZIP rather than a source-code clone.

```bat
cd /d C:\Users\Marsel\Desktop\apiM

```

Verify:

```bat
type .env.local
```

Expected:

```text
APIM_GHIDRA_HOME=C:\Users\Marsel\Desktop\apiM\tools\ghidra
```

Keep it out of Git:

```bat
echo .env.local>>.git/info/exclude
```

Then open a **new Command Prompt** and run:

```bat
java -version
cd /d C:\Users\Marsel\Desktop\apiM
rmdir /s /q .next
npm run dev
```

Next.js automatically loads `.env.local`; no additional enable switch is needed.

That environment report is wrong because it checked from the **agent command sandbox**, not the apiM server process.

The sandbox intentionally receives a scrubbed environment:

```text
APIM_GHIDRA_HOME = empty
```

That prevents model-run commands from inheriting host configuration and secrets. But `inspect_binary` runs server-side, where Next.js loads `.env.local`.

Also:

- `analyzeHeadless.bat` does not need to be on `PATH`.
- apiM uses the absolute path from `APIM_GHIDRA_HOME`.
- An `exit code 1` proves the launcher was found and started.
- A genuinely missing launcher produces `ENOENT`, not exit code 1.

This is a corrupted `.next` development cache, usually caused by deleting `.next` while a Next dev process is still running. It is unrelated to Ghidra or application source.

The “Next.js stale” badge only means a newer Next version exists; it is not the cause.

## Clean restart

Stop the process listening on port 3000:

```bat
powershell -NoProfile -Command "Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort 3000 -State Listen -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | ForEach-Object { Stop-Process -Id $_.OwningProcess -Force }"
```

Then:

```bat
cd /d C:\Users\Marsel\Desktop\apiM
rmdir /s /q .next
npm install
npm run dev
```

After it says `Ready`, hard-refresh the browser with:

```text
Ctrl+Shift+R
```

Do not delete `.next` while `npm run dev` is still running; that removes runtime chunks from underneath the active server and produces exactly this error.

If it still appears after this clean restart, stop the server and run:

```bat
rmdir /s /q node_modules
rmdir /s /q .next
npm ci
npm run dev
```

Do not delete `package-lock.json`.

Good—this is now an exact server-environment bug in apiM.

`inspect_binary` deliberately launches external analyzers with a minimal environment, but that list omitted `APPDATA`. Ghidra uses `%APPDATA%` for its Java-home cache/config and then fails JDK discovery even though `java.exe` is available interactively. This is ours to fix, not another installation problem.

I’m checking Ghidra 12.1.2’s launcher variables, then I’ll pass only the required Windows profile/JDK variables without exposing API keys or the full server environment.

Confirmed: this was an apiM server-environment bug.

### Exact cause

apiM launches Ghidra with a restricted environment. It passed:

- `PATH`
- `JAVA_HOME`
- `USERPROFILE`
- `LOCALAPPDATA`

But omitted:

```text
APPDATA
```

Ghidra 12’s `LaunchSupport` uses `%APPDATA%` to save/read its selected JDK. Without it:

```text
java.io.FileNotFoundException: "APPDATA" environment variable is not set
ERROR: Failed to find a supported JDK.
```

Java itself was installed correctly.

USER:
**Ghidra: ❌ still failing, but now with a *precise, fixable* error**

The good news is Ghidra **launched**. The log shows full headless startup (`Headless startup complete (2502 ms)`, scripts loaded, everything healthy). It dies on one line:

code**Copy**

```
ERROR Abort due to Headless analyzer error:
Path element starting with '.' is not permitted
java.lang.IllegalArgumentException
    at ghidra.util.NamingUtilities.checkName
    at ghidra.framework.protocol.ghidra.GhidraURL.checkValidProjectPath

```

**What this means**

Ghidra refuses project paths where **any directory name starts with a dot** (a hidden folder, `.something`). The apiM harness is creating its temp Ghidra project inside a dot-prefixed path — that's the *only* thing blocking it now. Ghidra itself is fine; the path being handed to it is not.

**The fix is on the apiM server side**, one of two ways:

1. **Change the project path** — make the Ghidra temp project live somewhere with no dot-element in the path, e.g. `C:\Users\Marsel\AppData\Local\ghidra-projects\...` instead of anything under a `.`-folder.
2. **If the dot comes from a workspace/config value** — look for where the harness builds the `-project` argument and strip any hidden directory from it.

Ghidra's `NamingUtilities.checkName` rejects *any* element starting with `.`, so this is a path sanitization issue, not a version or install issue.

That error identifies the exact remaining path bug: apiM currently creates the temporary Ghidra project as:

```text
.../analysis/<hash>/.ghidra-project
```

The dot-prefixed basename is ours, and Ghidra rejects it before import. I’m moving temporary projects completely outside the workspace to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\apiM\ghidra-projects\<hash>` (or the OS temp directory), where no hidden path component exists.

I’m also addressing the five-minute wait at the mechanism level:

1. `force_decompile` will stop rerunning already-cached full strings, entropy, carving, and capa.
2. On missing `CreateMove`/`IN_JUMP` names, Ghidra will first decompile callers of high-interest loader/process-memory APIs.
3. Only if that focused behavioral fallback finds nothing will it perform bounded full decompilation.
4. Cache profile changes will invalidate prior empty/path-failed Ghidra runs.

[STEP-START] {"type":"step-start"}
Confirmed: the Ghidra project path was the exact bug.

apiM created:

```text
.../analysis/<hash>/.ghidra-project
```

Ghidra rejects any path component beginning with `.`.

## Fix implemented

Temporary projects now use:

```text
%TEMP%\apim-ghidra-projects\<hash>
```

On your machine, that will resolve somewhere under:

```text
C:\Users\Marsel\AppData\Local\Temp\apim-ghidra-projects\
```

No dot-prefixed directory is involved. The temporary project is removed after analysis.

## Speed improvements

The five-minute wait had three causes:

1. `force_decompile` reran strings, entropy, carving and capa.
2. Missing `CreateMove`/`IN_JUMP` names immediately triggered full decompilation.
3. Ghidra automatic analysis could consume the whole four-minute timeout.

Now:

- `force_decompile` reruns **only Ghidra/ILSpy**.
- Strings, entropy, carving and capa remain cached.
- A focus miss first selects callers of:
  - `LoadLibrary`
  - `GetProcAddress`
  - `VirtualAlloc`
  - `WriteProcessMemory`
  - `CreateRemoteThread`
  - `CreateProcess`
  - related loader/process APIs
- Full decompilation happens only if that behavioral fallback also finds nothing.
- Packed-file automatic analysis defaults to **90 seconds**.
- Ordinary small-file automatic analysis defaults to **120 seconds**.
- Old path-failed Ghidra caches are invalidated.

Yes. Right now the model can pass booleans, but omission defaults to “run almost everything,” which wastes time and does not match your intent.

I’ll change binary analysis to an explicit model-selected layer list:

```json
{"analyses":["decompile"]}
{"analyses":["strings"]}
{"analyses":["capa","carve"]}
{"analyses":["all"]}
```

Default omission will become the cheap PE summary only. The agent prompt/tool schema will map “test Ghidra” to decompile only, “dump strings” to strings only, and “check everything” to all layers. Static artifacts will cache incrementally, so asking for entropy later will add it without deleting or regenerating the earlier strings dump.

Implemented and pushed.

## New behavior

The AI now chooses the binary-analysis layers based on the request.

### “Test Ghidra”

```json
{
  "analyses": ["decompile"]
}
```

Runs only:

- Minimal PE parsing needed to identify native/.NET
- Ghidra or ILSpy

It does **not** run strings, entropy, carving, dependencies, or capa.

### “Dump all strings”

```json
{
  "analyses": ["strings"]
}
```

Runs only the full ASCII/UTF-16 strings layer.

### “Check entropy and carve payloads”

```json
{
  "analyses": ["entropy", "carve"]
}
```

### “Run capa”

```json
{
  "analyses": ["capa"]
}
```

### “Inspect its DLL dependencies”

```json
{
  "analyses": ["dependencies"]
}
```

### “Check everything”

```json
{
  "analyses": ["all"]
}
```

Expands to:

```text
summary
strings
entropy
carve
dependencies
capa
decompile
```

### Ambiguous request

If the model omits `analyses`, apiM now defaults to the cheap PE summary—not everything.

## Incremental caching

Layers are cached independently:

1. Ask for strings → strings are generated.
2. Later ask for entropy → entropy is added.
3. Existing strings remain untouched.
4. Ask to retest Ghidra with `force_decompile` → only Ghidra/ILSpy reruns.
5. Completed capa, strings, entropy and carving remain cached.

## Agent instruction

The system prompt now explicitly teaches:

```text
test Ghidra      → ["decompile"]
dump strings     → ["strings"]
test capa        → ["capa"]
carve payloads   → ["carve"]
check everything → ["all"]
```

The model can also start with summary and request additional layers in later rounds if the summary shows they are needed.

They are only used for display, so a stale rate misleads\n * rather than overcharges — worth re-checking if DeepSeek changes pricing.\n */\n\nexport interface ModelRates {\n  /** Cache-miss input, per 1M tokens. */\n  input: number;\n  /** Cache-hit input, per 1M tokens. */\n  cachedInput: number;\n  /** Output, per 1M tokens. */\n  output: number;\n}\n\nexport const MODEL_RATES: Record<string, ModelRates> = {\n  \"deepseek-v4-pro\": { input: 0.435, cachedInput: 0.003625, output: 0.87 },\n  \"deepseek-v4-flash\": { input: 0.14, cachedInput: 0.0028, output: 0.28 },\n};\n\nexport interface UsageLike {\n  prompt_tokens?: number;\n  completion_tokens?: number;\n  total_tokens?: number;\n  /** DeepSeek reports how much of the prompt hit its cache. */\n  prompt_cache_hit_tokens?: number;\n  prompt_cache_miss_tokens?: number;\n}\n\n/**\n * Estimate the cost of one exchange in USD.\n *\n * Returns null for an unknown model rather than guessing, so the UI can stay\n * silent instead of showing a number that might be wrong.\n */\nexport function estimateCost(\n  usage: UsageLike | null | undefined,\n  model: string\n): number | null {\n  if (!usage) return null;\n  const rates = MODEL_RATES[model];\n  if (!rates) return null;\n\n  const completion = usage.completion_tokens ?? 0;\n  const prompt = usage.prompt_tokens ?? 0;\n\n  // Prefer the reported cache split; fall back to treating everything as a miss.\n  const hit = usage.prompt_cache_hit_tokens ?? 0;\n  const miss = usage.prompt_cache_miss_tokens ?? Math.max(0, prompt - hit);\n\n  return (\n    (miss / 1e6) * rates.input +\n    (hit / 1e6) * rates.cachedInput +\n    (completion / 1e6) * rates.output\n  );\n}\n\n/** Format a cost for display, keeping very small amounts legible. */\nexport function formatCost(usd: number): string {\n  if (usd < 0.01) return `$${usd.toFixed(4)}`;\n  if (usd < 1) return `$${usd.toFixed(3)}`;\n  return `$${usd.toFixed(2)}`;\n}\n\n/** Format an elapsed duration compactly. */\nexport function formatDuration(ms: number): string {\n  if (ms < 1000) return `${Math.round(ms)}ms`;\n  const seconds = ms / 1000;\n  if (seconds < 60) return `${seconds.toFixed(1)}s`;\n  const minutes = Math.floor(seconds / 60);\n  return `${minutes}m ${Math.round(seconds % 60)}s`;\n}\n"},"callProviderMetadata":{"openai":{"itemId":"fc_0be099a60c14fb8e016a822fbb0a248199bf22ea906e601a6d"}}}

The measurements confirm the old optimizer is now pointed at the wrong economics:

- It hardcodes old Pro rates (`$0.435 / $0.003625 / $0.87`) in pricing tests, compaction break-even math, tree-cache simulations, and the cost lab.
- It deliberately keeps up to **80 old tool results verbatim** and waits until roughly **250k prompt tokens** before pruning.
- It waits until roughly **500k tokens** before folding old reasoning/tool rounds.
- Caveman reduces final prose, but agent cost is dominated by repeated reasoning, tool schemas, and retained tool results. On multi-round tasks, making the answer terse can even cause extra continuation/tool rounds, so output shrinks while total billed tokens rise.

I’ll preserve the plugin as the same final tail-position `system` message and optimize around it—not inside or above it.

Stopping at a\n *     round boundary means the work so far is saved and resumable.\n *\n *   - It predicts the next round rather than only checking the last one.
